definition: Intrinsic motivation is the inner drive to learn or gain new skills because of curiosity, interest, and a willingness to learn, rather than because of outside pressure. In school settings, higher intrinsic motivation is linked with benefits such as stronger engagement, better achievement and performance over time, and lower academic anxiety.

reasons: The definition claims intrinsic motivation is “rather than because of outside pressure,” but the packet only describes intrinsic motivation as a willingness to learn and being driven by curiosity and interest; it does not explicitly provide a contrast to outside pressure.

The definition claims “stronger engagement,” but the packet mentions academic benefits including STEM persistence and achievement/anxiety; it does not explicitly state stronger engagement as a linked benefit.

The definition states “better achievement and performance over time,” which is directionally supported by the packet’s mention of higher academic achievement and higher academic performance over time, but because other key claims (outside pressure contrast; stronger engagement) are not supported, the overall definition cannot be accepted as written.
